title: Props: a dozen pieces for a game
brief: Make twelve props for a small fantasy game, each as a model recipe in your work folder (one file a prop, under `assets/models/`), with one style for all of them. Sizes are in metres, +Y up, each prop standing on y = 0 and centred on the Y axis unless it says otherwise.
The props
1. A gear: a flat spur gear 0.4 wide and 0.06 thick, 16 teeth all alike and evenly spaced, with a round hole through its middle 0.08 across.
2. A heart pickup: a heart 0.3 wide and 0.05 thick with softly rounded edges, standing upright (its point down).
3. An arch: a round stone arch 2 wide and 2.5 tall, its opening 1.2 wide, 0.4 deep, standing on the ground.
4. A star badge: a five-pointed star 0.12 across, 0.01 thick, its points sharp.
5. A key: an old iron key 0.15 long: a ring bow, a round shaft and a bit with two teeth, as one piece.
6. A ring: a torus 0.025 across the middle of its band and 0.005 thick, lying flat.
7. A gem: a faceted gem 0.04 across with flat faces (a cut stone: a crown above, a pointed pavilion below), at least 16 faces.
8. A pill: a capsule 0.02 long and 0.008 across, lying along X.
9. A shield: a heater shield 0.6 tall and 0.45 wide, slightly curved front to back, 0.03 thick.
10. A column: a round column 3 tall and 0.4 across, with a square base and a square top slab each 0.5 wide and 0.12 tall.
11. A cog train: three gears of 10, 16 and 24 teeth of the same tooth size, side by side on one plane, each meshing with the next, in one recipe.
12. A lantern frame: an open frame 0.25 wide and 0.4 tall: four corner posts, a square base, a pyramid roof and a ring on top, as one recipe.
Checkable without hands
Someone who cannot open your files in a modelling program will check them, so offer two things for every prop, however you make them:

1. A headless build: one command that builds every recipe with no window and prints, as JSON, for each prop its name, its triangle count, whether it is closed (watertight) and its bounds (least and greatest x, y, z).
2. A frame: a PNG picture of each prop, 512 by 512, from the front and a little above, the whole prop in view.
Hand in, in your work folder
- The twelve recipes and the style they share.
- README.md: the exact commands for the headless build and the frames, and what you checked yourself and how.

acceptance.text: The headless build exists, builds all twelve recipes with no window and prints each one's name, triangle count, closedness and bounds as JSON.
A 512 x 512 PNG frame of each of the twelve props is written by the commands in README.md, with the whole prop in view.
The gear has 16 teeth, all alike and evenly spaced, a round hole through its middle, and bounds within 5% of 0.4 x 0.06 x 0.4.
The heart reads as a heart in its frame (two lobes on top, a point below) and its edges are rounded, not sharp.
The arch is about 2 wide and 2.5 tall with a round-topped opening about 1.2 wide that one can see through, and it is closed.
The star badge has five sharp points, evenly spaced, and is about 0.12 across and 0.01 thick.
The key has a ring bow with a hole, a round shaft and a bit with two teeth, and is about 0.15 long.
The ring is a torus lying flat, about 0.025 across its band's middle line, with a hole through it.
The gem has at least 16 flat faces, a crown above and a pointed pavilion below, and is about 0.04 across.
The pill is a capsule with round ends, about 0.02 long along X and 0.008 across.
The shield is a heater shape (a flat top, sides that curve to a point below), curved front to back, about 0.6 tall and 0.45 wide.
The column is round, about 3 tall and 0.4 across, with a square base and a square top slab each about 0.5 wide.
The cog train has three gears of 10, 16 and 24 teeth of one tooth size, whose teeth mesh without overlapping in the frame.
The lantern frame has four corner posts, a square base, a pyramid roof and a ring on top, and is open between the posts.
Every one of the twelve recipes builds closed (watertight) as the headless build reports, and the props share one style.
README.md gives commands for the two checks that work as written from a fresh start.
